wintun.distribution: No separate Wintun file is shipped in round 2. The pinned sing-tun (github.com/metacubex/sing-tun v0.4.22, internal/wintun/amd64/wintun.dll) embeds the official DLL byte for byte and loads it from memory, so there is no DLL search path, PATH or current-directory lookup to attack. scripts/test-native-windows.py --suite core fails if that embedded file ever differs from amd64_dll_sha256.
wintun.license_note: Source is GPL-2.0; the prebuilt signed DLLs carry a more permissive license that ships inside the ZIP. The project says the signed DLLs are the only supported way to distribute Wintun. Clause 3(d) of that license allows redistribution 'alongside other software that uses the Software only via the Permitted API' (wintun.h) and forbids extracting from or modifying the Software: round 8 must have the legal review decide whether the in-memory embedding by sing-tun is acceptable for a commercial installer, or ship the unmodified wintun.dll from the ZIP next to the Core and load it from the protected install directory.
wintun.verified: 2026-10-13 (round 2): ZIP downloaded from wintun.net into an empty directory, SHA-256 equals the published value; amd64/wintun.dll inside it equals the DLL embedded in sing-tun v0.4.22; the DLL's certificate strings name Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher / Microsoft Windows Third Party Component CA 2012. Authenticode validity is checked by Get-AuthenticodeSignature on Windows in .github/workflows/windows.yml (step 'Embedded Wintun DLL is the signed official build').

installer.license_note: The vendor asks commercial users to purchase a license. Budget for it before the release round.

ci.note: GitHub-hosted runners offer no x64 Windows 10/11 client image (only Arm64 Windows 11). CI proves build, unit tests and that the binaries start on a real x64 Windows host. It does NOT prove Windows 10/11 client compatibility, UAC, SCM install, Wintun or networking.

os_support.build_floor: Windows 10 2004 (build 19041), enforced at compile time by the net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0 target
os_support.promise_rule: A system is only promised to customers after it passes the Windows suites on a real machine of that system. Until then it is 'intended', not 'supported'.
os_support.same_binary: One win-x64 binary serves both systems; nothing Windows 11-only is used, and nothing Windows 10-only is used at the cost of Windows 11.
os_support.microsoft_position: The official .NET 10 supported-OS list (updated 2026-09-28) names Windows 11 23H2/24H2/25H2/26H1 and only Windows 10 21H2/1809/1607 Enterprise/IoT editions; Windows 10 22H2 is not listed and Windows 10 left mainstream support on 2025-10-14. 'Not listed' means Microsoft does not test it, not that it is known to fail; first-hand testing on Windows 10 22H2 decides.
